answer: Behavioral Trajectory Clustering. Agents log action sequences; a detector clusters accounts by near-identical timing and task-order fingerprints. When a cluster exceeds a threshold, all members are flagged and their rewards withheld pending review. Each flagged identity then costs an attacker a full audit cycle plus forfeited earnings, and the opal-tier fee for re-entry after a confirmed match.
